tasks.title: Additive index-only Alembic revision 004_rollup_query_indexes.py

tasks.reason: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) over all 11 rebuild queries at 160k rows. Finding: D-04's proposed ix_usage_events_ts is NEVER selected by the planner for any of the 11 queries — plans byte-identical to baseline, and still not chosen under enable_seqscan=off. Two independent reasons: the 3 org-wide aggregates have no WHERE (100% selectivity, seq scan is physically correct), and date_trunc(text,timestamptz,text) is STABLE not IMMUTABLE so a matching expression index cannot legally be created. ix_usage_events_ts therefore EXCLUDED. Shipped instead, on measured evidence: ix_usage_events_program_id_covering (program_id) INCLUDE (total, lines_added), which turns _build_org_summary from a heap-touching Index Scan into an Index Only Scan — Heap Fetches 0, buffers 61,681 -> 967, ~60ms -> ~33ms, reproduced over two runs. All 7 program-scope queries were already index-backed, unchanged. revises=003_program_roster; downgrade drops exactly that one index; upgrade->downgrade->upgrade round-trip verified, schema otherwise identical. ruff/format/mypy clean. See AF-05/AF-06.

tasks.title: Measure rewritten rebuild latency + contention_wait_ms under AC-1 four-program concurrency at 20k/160k rows
tasks.notes: Measurement-only task, no source file changes. Runs T-02's four-program concurrent fixture against T-03's rewritten, T-04-indexed implementation at 20k and 160k total rows; records p50/p95 duration per function and contention_wait_ms per call pair. Record the measured figures in this task's completion `reason` field — T-07 consumes them directly; no separate scratch file.
tasks.reason:
MEASURED (orchestrator ran this inline; subagents were rate-limited). Postgres 16 @5442, migrated to 004 incl. ix_usage_events_program_id_covering. 7 reps per function per size.
CONFOUNDED RUN (total and in-program grown together, 4-program round-robin):
  rebuild_program_rollups  20k total/5k in-prog  p50 414.2ms p95 455.6ms
                          160k total/40k in-prog p50 3581.8ms p95 3645.0ms
  rebuild_org_rollups       20k  p50 66.0ms  p95 71.2ms | 160k  p50 445.4ms  p95 489.0ms
  concurrent x4 wall: 1441.2ms @20k, 11315.7ms @160k; errors=0 at both sizes
  contention_wait_ms distinct per call: {4,11,12} @20k, {3,4,6,9} @160k -> max 12ms, negligible
AC-5 ISOLATION (in-program HELD at 5,000 rows, total grown 8x) — this is the run that settles AC-5:
   20k total  p50 442.8ms  p95 525.4ms
  160k total  p50 452.3ms  p95 608.5ms
  => +2% p50 for 8x total growth. rebuild_program_rollups is FLAT in total history. AC-5 MET.
VERDICT: AC-4 met (org 8.7x faster at 160k: 3864ms->445ms, comfortably inside any share of the 3s ceiling; it still grows with total, unavoidably, since it aggregates the whole table, and AC-4 requires meeting a budget not flatness). AC-5 met on its literal wording (no tracking of TOTAL history). BUT see AF-08: the program rebuild still scales ~linearly with a single program's OWN accumulated rows (5k->40k in-prog = 414ms->3582ms), so p95 3645ms at 40k in-program EXCEEDS ING-02's entire end-to-end p95<=3s ceiling on its own. The story's NFR intent ("holds its latency budget forever instead of degrading on every push") is therefore only partly achieved.

tasks.title: Pin replacement rebuild budget + engine timeout from T-06's measurement; preflight-validate
tasks.notes: Implements D-02/D-03. tasks.reason: Orchestrator ran inline (subagents rate-limited). PINNED FROM MEASUREMENT, not guessed: _STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, _CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S=10, as hardcoded module constants per D-03. Derivation: the slowest INDIVIDUAL statement in the worst-case rebuild is 97.9ms (a chunked user_sessions INSERT at 40k in-program) — the multi-second rebuild total is the sum of many such chunked writes, not one long statement, so the statement bound need not be seconds. 5000ms = ~51x headroom. Deliberately set ABOVE freshness.py's existing 3.0s call-site asyncio.wait_for so that tighter bound still fires first (research risk #8: avoids two competing exceptions for one slow query). Risk #3 is structurally void: migrations/env.py builds its own engine via async_engine_from_config and tests/conftest.py builds its own, so neither inherits this timeout — a long CREATE INDEX cannot trip it. AC-7 VERIFIED ENFORCED: SHOW statement_timeout returns 5s and SELECT pg_sleep(8) raises psycopg QueryCanceled. PREFLIGHT found and fixed a real defect T-04 left behind: migration 004 created the covering index but never declared it in model metadata, so this project's schema-diff gate (TestSchemaDiffGate) and its constraints fixture both failed. Adding an index here requires THREE files, not one — see AF-09. Final: 505 passed, 0 failed; ruff clean; mypy clean across 120 files.
